statement: For every positive integer n, define S_0(n)={1,...,floor(n/2)}, S_(j+1)(n)={n mod k : k in S_j(n), k>0}, and s_j(n)=|S_j(n)|, with repeated values counted once and zero retained as a value but excluded as a modulus. Then s_2(n)/n has no limit as n tends to infinity through the positive integers. More precisely, let M=691374732709966591241323368000, L=75600, alpha=30093341768093808664597/276977102566985955634500, and beta=1182869/9979200. For every integer t>=1, s_2(M*t)/(M*t)<=alpha+(M+3)/(M*t) and s_2(L*t+1)/(L*t+1)>=beta-(L+2)/(L*t+1). Consequently the first subsequence has limsup at most alpha and the second has liminf at least beta, with beta-alpha=131410063319607383019139/13294900923215325870456000>0. For all t>=203 the same bounds separate uniformly: defining A=(M+3)/M and B=(L+2)/L, the upper constant is alpha+A/203, the lower constant is beta-B/203, and their gap is 559612671694976819161613011/17543633842515402252748580463000>0. Scope is exactly j=2; neither higher iterates nor exact global liminf/limsup values are asserted.
contribution: A complete proposed proof of the frozen j=2 nonconvergence problem using an exact quotient-congruence characterization, uniform finite-cutoff errors, and two explicit arithmetic progressions with rational separation. This answers the j=2 specialization of Baraskar and Vukusic's Problem 2, beyond their general iterate bounds. The full argument and exact arithmetic are supplied for fresh referee review; no acceptance is claimed. No equivalent result was found in the bounded primary-literature screen on 2026-09-12, without an exhaustive priority guarantee.
